speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; have these episodes been witnessed by anyone, and if so, exactly what movements or sounds did they observe? Additionally, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus secondary to Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (JME). The patient's presentation of staring, hand gestures (myoclonus), post-ictal confusion, and a specific "muddy taste" (gustatory aura) is classic for generalized epileptic seizures. The duration of 3-4 minutes and lack of recall suggests prolonged absence status rather than typical brief absence seizures.
